title: ADAPTIVE OPTICAL LENSES FOR COMPACT OPTICAL CORRECTIONS IN SMALL SATELLITE PAYLOADS - EXPRO PLUS
description: One of the challenges facing many compact optical payloads (imaging, spectrographic, Lidar, etc.) is identifying ways to maintain performance whilereducing the payload size and power that they can fit on ever-smaller satellite platforms. Active correction systems for medium or large size instruments aremainly based on deformable mirrors (either primary mirror or conjugate of the entrance pupil on the instrument). These are very efficient correction tools butmay require a volume and power not compatible with smaller payloads such as small or nano satellites.An alternative to this approach is the use of adaptive lenses which can be implemented inside the optical layout without need for e.g. high-quality pupilreimaging. Adaptive lenses have achieved a good level of maturity in on-ground applications (e.g. microscopy, beam shaping, telescope systems, etc.) but haveyet to be considered for space applications. By nature, the COTS aspect of adaptive lenses would allow to use them for mass-produced nano or small satellites at a competitive price. The correction abilities could range from compensation of thermo-elastic deformation affecting image quality (low-order aberrations), to line-of-sight compensation of thermally-induced drifts, to staring function implementation allowing to compensate satellite motion to increase integration time.The proposed activity aims at developing an engineering model of an adaptive optical lens suitable for compact instruments for small satellites. The adaptivelens will be analysed in terms of components and materials to adapt them to the space environment, in particular, interfaces to the payload, space radiation andvacuum. The following tasks are foreseen in the frame of this activity: Identification of a target payload and platform and the consolidation of requirements for an optical payload. Analysis of changes required to the existing product (drive electronics and adaptive lens). Breadboarding and testing of materials to identify sensitivity to radiation and vacuum environments. Detailed design of the adaptive optical lens engineering model. Manufacturing of the engineering model. Verification and testing in a relevant environment including in a complete telescope set-up.

title: A framework for the systematic comparison between the DSA Transparency reports & the DSA Transparency Database submissions
description:
The objective of the support contract is to develop a systematic framework to compare and benchmark the data generated through the two main content moderation transparency data sources of the DSA: the transparency reports and the DSA Transparency Database. 

To test and apply this framework, the support contract will develop a methodology to compare the data reported in one cycle of VLOPs and VLOSEs’ transparency reports with their statements of reasons submissions to the DSA Transparency Database in the same timeframe to check for (in)consistencies in the reporting. In performing this comparison, the support contract should take into account (differences in) the relevant legal bases of the two data sources and document the comparative methodology developed for future use. The comparison should be made using the reports that will be published according to the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2835 of 4 November 2024 and the updated Transparency Database schema.

The focus of the support contract should be on developing meaningful, per-platform quantitative indicators reports published in the covered timeframe., The support contract should also propose operational recommendations for compliance monitoring, including recommendations for future schema updates to the DSA Transparency Database or improvements to the Transparency Reports’' templates. 

The insights gained from this support contract will support the Commission in its supervision and enforcement work.

description: Предметът на настоящата обществена поръчка е свързан със създаването на STEM среда в СУ "Свети Патриарх Евтимий"- гр. Пловдив, която цели прилагането на иновативни подходи за обучение, в нетрадиционна учебна среда, която би подпомогнало образователния процес в посока мотивация и успеваемост. Проектът предвижда доизграждане на STEM центрове в направления "Природни науки" и "Математика и Информатика" и ще обхваща предмети „Биология и здравно образование“ (БЗО), „Физика и астрономия“ (ФА), „Химия и опазване на околната среда“ (ХООС), „Информационни технологии“, "Информатика" и "Математика“. Училищният STEM център ще бъде ситуиран в шест класни стаи и коридор на втория етаж в сградата на училището. Всички архитектурни и интериорни решения ще бъдат изпълнени с фокус върху подходящи материали и дизайн за отделните зони и пространства по иновативен начин, осигуряващ творческа и креативна обстановка. Строително монтажните работи включват преработка на съществуващи ел. инсталации, подмяна на настилки и врати, очукване мазилки, шпакловане, боядисване на стени и други съпътстващи ремонта дейности съгласно приложената количествена сметка. Обществената поръчка се финансира в рамките на процедура за предоставяне на средства от Механизма за възстановяване и устойчивост, Стълб „Иновативна България“, Компонент 1 „Образование и умения“, Инвестиция 1 „Центрове за НТИМ и иновации в образованието“, процедура чрез директно предоставяне на средства на конкретни крайни получатели BG-RRP-1.015 „Училищна STEM среда“ по Национален план за възстановяване и устойчивост на Република България, финансирано от Европейския съюз – NextGenerationEU. description: Im Außenbereich der Arche Nebra und auf dem Weg zum Fundort der Himmelsscheibe werden fünf Timscopes montiert. Die Timescopes bilden dabei die Verbindung zwischen Parkplatz, Arche und Fundort. Mit dem Blick in die Vergangenheit kann der Besucher vertiefende Geschichten zur Umgebung der Arche erfahren. Die fest montierten Fernrohre präsentieren die bildlichen Geschichten in Form von 3D gefrästen, hinterleuchteten Bildern. Als Grundlage der Bilder werden fünf Szenen als hinterleuchtetes Papierdiorama gefertigt welche als Grundlage für die Fräs- und Bilddateien dienen. Die einzelnen Dioramen werden in einem 16:9 Seitenverhältnis gefertigt und müssen min. eine tiefe von 300 mm aufweisen. Alle Dioramen sind aus geschöpftem Papier zu fertigen, welche die Detailtiefe erst durch die Hinterleuchtung erfahrbar macht. Der Bauraum ist mit min 10 Ebenen zu bespielen. Die Breite und Höher der Dioramen kann dem Inhalt angepasst werden, jedoch sollte die mindestgröße 1000 x 600 mm aufweißen. Alle 5 Dioramen sollen dieselbe Detailtiefe aufweisen. Die künstlerische Umsetzung hat dabei immer in der direkten Abstimmung mit den Mitarbeitern der Arche und dem Planer zu erfolgen. Teil der Leistung ist das Erstellen der Dioramen, sowie die Vorbereitung der fertigen Dioramen zur Bilderstellung inkl. Ausleuchtung. Nach der Datenerstellung ist beabsichtigt die Dioramen in einer Sonderausstellung in der Arche zu präsentieren und anschließend zu Archivieren.
